notes_for_editor: Much of the narrative rests on LighthouseFriends (secondary, copyrighted; paraphrased) because the corpus has no Light-House Board volumes before 1891 and the newspaper searches (Chronicling America) returned nothing usable in the time budget. The 1851 inspection report, the 1876 reprimand, the 1877 inspection and the 1905 mud-hen and Pusey items are all second-hand via LighthouseFriends. The 1897 and 1900 report page numbers were not verified. First-tower height disagrees (75 ft NRHP, 70 ft LF, 88 ft Cape May Magazine, omitted from story). Lighting date: Halloween vs Halloween Eve. The 1936 Bulletin gives a 12-panel lens, the 1859 lens was 16 panels per LF; unexplained. Wikipedia says Belle Palmer became custodian of the lighthouse in 1933; not included because no non-Wikipedia source was read. NRHP gives 175 ft as height (it is the focal height). Lightning of 1891 is in the fiscal-1891 report (June 1891 falls inside FY ended 30 June 1891). Keeper roster follows USLHS; LighthouseFriends roster is identical. LighthouseFriends spells Foster as 'Downes' in the text and 'Downs' in the list, and 'Commander Brigman' in 1877 (not named in story). Fact-check 2026-10-27: NRHP tells the 1847 move differently (1823 tower rebuilt on Great Island) from LighthouseFriends (new second tower); now stated in the story. USLHS gives 'Year Original Lens Installed: 1853' against LighthouseFriends' 1859 first-order lens; not used in the story. The 1927 efficiency flag year is LighthouseFriends'; the Bulletin index gives page numbers only. Ownership is LighthouseFriends' (possibly dated). 1891 report entry is on printed p. 77.
